builds.name: classic6-20b
builds.caption: Four sticky pistons, two on each side of the opening, each hold one door block in the opening while they are extended. The lever sits on the frame above the door and powers the frame's blocks, partly through a line of dust. Flip the lever off and the pistons pull the blocks into the wall.

builds.caption: A hopper clock: set its time from 1 second to about 4 minutes by how many items you put in the first hopper (each item adds 0.8 s: 2 items = 1 s, 7 = 5 s, 76 = 1 min 0.2 s, 320 = 4 min 15 s), 13 blocks. Two hoppers facing each other pass the items one per 8 gt; each hopper's comparator lights a dust on the block in front of it, which powers a sticky piston; the two pistons hold one redstone block over the hopper that receives (a locked hopper still receives) and the sender's piston pulls it back over the sender when the sender runs empty. Period 16 N - 12 gt for N items (any stackable item; 5 stacks of 64 at most). The output (the lamp cell west of the first comparator's block) is on all the time but one short gap a period.

builds.name: clk-misc-daylight-spit
builds.caption: A daylight sensor sees the sky; a piston covers and uncovers it, so its reading flips every second while the sun is up. In detail: an inverted daylight detector reads 0 under the open sky and 1 when a block hides the sky right above it (sky light 14 from the sides). It updates only when the game time is a multiple of 20 gt. An observer on it pulses a sticky piston (through the stone under the piston) for 2 gt: a 2 gt pulse makes a sticky piston spit the block in front of it one cell further (here: over the detector) and the next pulse pull it back (the block 2 cells away is no longer moving). So every detector update toggles the cover and the next update (20 gt later) sees the change: P = 40 gt.

builds.caption: Dropper ring (clk-item): a hopper ring with dropper(s) in its bottom row; the comparator in the inner column reads the top-row hopper above it and fires the dropper below it (through the repeaters, each on stone). The ring runs counter-clockwise; P = 20 + 14 (W - 3) + 7 (depth - 3) + 7 [one dropper] + 2 x (sum of repeater delays): fourteen cards of this ring (one per P mod 14) reach every P from 42 up.

P = 3 x 15. A1 is out of S3's range (dist^2 257), so after the kick only S2 wakes; afterwards the sensor two hops ahead is always still in its 20 gt dead time. Kick: right-click the note block K (only S1 is within 16 of it; S1 faces east so its back, K, gets no power from it).

builds.name: clk-rt-count7-k2-over-fade114
builds.caption: Comparator COUNTER over another clock (clk-rt): a lossless comparator ring (2 + 2 comparators, one in subtract mode) loses 2 level(s) per pulse of the inner clock (its pulse cut to strength 2 by a subtract comparator with side 13) and its torch refills it to 14 at 0: period = 7 inner periods. Inner clock: Comparator FADING ring (clk-rt): two dust (one level lost per lap) -> top row [comparator, comparator] -> block F -> dust beside F (a wall torch on F lights when the ring is empty and refills it through a dust beside it) -> bottom row [comparator, comparator] -> back; the compare-mode comparators keep a signal strength, each dust-to-dust step loses one level per lap, and the torch refills the ring at 0

builds.name: hopclk-sealed-p1200
builds.caption: A clock that pulses exactly every 1 minute, set by the 38 stones in its first hopper, and sealed: no dropped item can reach its hoppers. Two hoppers facing each other pass the stones one per 8 gt; each hopper's comparator powers a sticky piston, and the two pistons hold one redstone block beside the hopper that receives (a locked hopper still receives) until the sender is empty; a stone covers each hopper. A repeater in one piston's path holds the redstone block a few ticks longer, which trims the time to exactly 1 minute. Copper bulbs (each toggled once per cycle and read by a comparator) double the time per bulb. Catalog parts: comparators, a repeater delay, copper-bulb T flip-flops as dividers.

builds.name: pulse-fall-sculk-filter-L10
builds.caption: One 10-tick pulse (half a second) every time the input turns OFF, even after the shortest input (2 ticks), and footsteps or dropped items nearby never set it off: the input opens a trapdoor and closes it when it turns off, a calibrated sculk sensor (a sound sensor) switches on for exactly 10 ticks when it hears the trapdoor close, and a comparator reading a chest tunes the sensor to closing sounds only. To build it: fill the chest with 988 items that stack to 64 (15 full stacks and 28 more), so the comparator gives 9 (the number shown over the chest in the 3D view). Good to know: the trapdoor clacks on every edge, and each clack is a vibration that sets off other sculk sensors within 16 blocks; the sensor still hears other machines' closing sounds within 16 blocks (a door or trapdoor closing, a piston pulling back, a lever or button switched off); "vibration-proof" means proof against players walking, jumping, dropping, placing and breaking blocks around it. The first falling-edge detector that sees the shortest inputs (2 ticks). Detail: a trapdoor emits block_open (frequency 10) and block_close (9); a calibrated sensor with a back signal accepts that frequency only (a lever's switch-off is 9 too, on the same edge).

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
metrics: 2 gt (the shortest a real input makes)

builds.name: pulse-rise-sculk-filter-L10
builds.caption: One 10-tick pulse (half a second) every time the input turns on, even for the shortest input (2 ticks), and footsteps or dropped items nearby never set it off: the input makes a note block play, a calibrated sculk sensor (a sound sensor) hears it and switches on for exactly 10 ticks, and a comparator reading a chest tunes the sensor to that one kind of sound. To build it: fill the chest with 1111 items that stack to 64 (17 full stacks and 23 more), so the comparator gives 10 (the number shown over the chest in the 3D view). Good to know: the note block sounds on every rising edge, and that sound is a vibration that sets off other sculk sensors within 16 blocks; the sensor still hears other machines' sounds of the same kind within 16 blocks (another note block, a door or trapdoor opening, a piston pushing, a lever or button switched on); "vibration-proof" means proof against players walking, jumping, dropping, placing and breaking blocks around it. Detail: the note block plays only when it becomes powered (note_block_play, frequency 10); a calibrated sensor with a back signal accepts that frequency only (the lever's block_deactivate is 9, footsteps 1, items landing 2, blocks broken or placed 12 and 13).

metrics: 2 gt (the shortest a real input makes)

builds.name: pulse-oneshot-rise
builds.caption: One pulse of 18, 34, 50... ticks every time the input turns on: a piston-moved observer lights a copper bulb and a loop of repeaters switches it off; each extra row adds 16 ticks. Detail: extendable family oneshot-rise (n = 0): rising-edge with L = 18 + 16n gt, 17 + 4n blocks. a sticky piston pushes an observer whose back then faces a copper bulb; the observer fires on landing and lights the bulb; a comparator reads the bulb into a U of delay-4 repeaters that comes back into the bulb and turns it off one loop later (a bulb toggles only on rising edges of its power, so the loop's own falling edge does nothing); on the falling edge the observer is pulled back and fires into nothing. Extension: lengthen the repeater U by one row: one more delay-4 repeater (on stone) in each column. Generator: mctas circuit pulse family oneshot-rise --n N --out FILE.

builds.name: pulse-limiter-sculk-filter-L10
builds.caption: Cuts any input down to exactly 10 ticks (half a second), however long it is held (shorter inputs come out as 10 ticks too), and footsteps or dropped items nearby never set it off: the input makes a note block play, a calibrated sculk sensor (a sound sensor) hears it and switches on for exactly 10 ticks, and a comparator reading a chest tunes the sensor to that one kind of sound. To build it: fill the chest with 1111 items that stack to 64 (17 full stacks and 23 more), so the comparator gives 10 (the number shown over the chest in the 3D view). Good to know: the note block sounds on every input, and that sound is a vibration that sets off other sculk sensors within 16 blocks; the sensor still hears other machines' sounds of the same kind within 16 blocks (another note block, a door or trapdoor opening, a piston pushing, a lever or button switched on); "vibration-proof" means proof against players walking, jumping, dropping, placing and breaking blocks around it. Detail: the note block plays only when it becomes powered (note_block_play, frequency 10); a calibrated sensor with a back signal accepts that frequency only (the lever's block_deactivate is 9, footsteps 1, items landing 2, blocks broken or placed 12 and 13).

circuit.claim: smallest for its size of 2 tested
metrics: 2 gt (the shortest a real input makes)
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: pulse-limiter-sculk-filter-L10 pulse-limiter L 10 gt, delay 1 gt, min-pulse 2 gt (the shortest a real input makes), vibration-proof yes, 5 blocks, 2x2x4, robust

builds.caption: A 5-tick delay in 11 blocks: the signal comes out exactly 5 ticks later on both edges, which a repeater line (even ticks only) cannot do. The input pushes a redstone block (top left) next to the middle piston and, through a repeater set to 1, makes the piston behind it push a second block next to the same piston from the other side 2 ticks later; the middle piston fires 1 tick after the first block lands (a piston always waits a tick after a block arrives), and the second block keeps it out until 2 ticks after the input falls. It pushes away the redstone block that holds the output piston (top right) extended, so that piston pulls its own block next to the output 5 ticks after the rise; when the middle piston pulls the block back, the output piston waits its tick again and pushes its block away 5 ticks after the fall.

builds.name: counter45-items
builds.caption: Counter 45, 23 blocks, with items (track memory, `mctas circuit memory items --n 45`): the output toggles once every 45 pulses, and the same 23 blocks count any N up to 576; only the number of items loaded changes. Two droppers face each other and hold 45 items between them; each pulse fires only one of them, so the pile walks from one to the other and each runs empty once every 45 pulses. A comparator reads each dropper, and the torch on its output block is lit exactly while that dropper is empty; both torches touch the copper bulb, which therefore toggles each time a dropper runs empty. The bulb is the phase: a comparator reading it powers the stone under the left dropper, which holds it (a dropper kept powered sees no new pulse), and through a dust under the right dropper switches off the torch beside it, which held the right one. The pulse reaches the right dropper through the input block on its lid and the left one through a dust on its own lid.

builds.name: pext-n2-flat-flipsafe10-6x4
builds.caption: A 2-piston extender you can flip back at any time, sideways and one block thick (10 blocks, 6x4x1): the block goes out 2 cells in 9 gt and back in 15 gt, and turning the lever off or on again early never strands a block. How it works: the lever drives the back sticky piston, which pushes a second sticky piston and a slime frame carrying a third sticky piston, the block and an observer. Each time the frame lands, its observer gives the third piston a short pulse through the slime: going out it pushes the block one more cell and leaves it there; coming back it pulls the block home. On the way back the back piston only pulls the second piston home; an observer above that piston sees it arrive and gives it a short pulse that reaches the frame and pulls it home. builds.name: shulker-loader-1wide-1x6x11-36b
builds.caption: A one-block-wide shulker loader you can line up side by side with no gap (36 blocks, 1x6x11): a dispenser under the box spot places an empty box, the hopper above fills it from the items chest, and when the box is full a piston behind it breaks it; the dropped full box lands on the hopper under the box's front, which sends it to the output chest. How it works: a comparator reads the box and a copper bulb toggles once per full box; the comparator reading the bulb starts a chain of sticky pistons and observers over the top that ends at a dropper above the breaking piston, and the observer under that dropper fires the piston. A comparator on the first hopper of the box line (it sees a box arrive even one at a time, or from a chest kept full) and the observer next to the breaker both fire a dispenser block; a sticky piston then moves an observer down, and observers and droppers pass the pulse to a dropper under the box dispenser, which fires it without touching the hoppers beside it. It passes the judge's full-chest, endless-supply, one-box and one-box burst checks. Found by `mctas circuit shulker anneal --sweep 23,29,37` (every trickle phase required) from the 41-block 1x6x11 loader (pext).

builds.caption: One TNT per BUTTON press (site QA 2026-10-21: a real button holds 20-30 gt, so the 16-block engine judged with a 4-tick removal of its holding redstone block lit several TNT per press). The engine of tnt-triggered-launch-16b with a one-shot hold instead: the obsidian beside the piston is strongly powered by a wall torch under it, which holds the piston; the torch hangs on the stone under the piston (in the obsidian foot's place) and the button is on that stone. A press powers the stone: the stone holds the piston itself and the torch goes dark. At the release the stone goes quiet 2 ticks before the torch relights: the piston drops, the frame comes back, its redstone block repowers the piston through the dust and the push lights ONE TNT, however long the press. Latency: the press, then 5 ticks.

builds.name: bud-slime-qc
builds.caption: The classic BUD: it sees blocks placed, removed or changed next to the target and pure block updates, which no observer can see: the smallest, 3 blocks. A sticky piston under a slime block and a redstone block is powered without having noticed it (the power reaches it only through the block above it, called quasi-connectivity); the first update makes it notice and lift the redstone block past the output for a moment, then pull it back, armed again. Detail: the landing slime block updates the piston through its head so it retracts, the redstone block landing last, so it re-arms without an update. A change by shape alone sends no block update: not detected; two updates 2 ticks apart jam it.

builds.name: mono-retrig-ring-L12
builds.caption: Gives a 12-tick output pulse after each input pulse, and a new input restarts the 12 ticks: every input refills a small two-comparator loop that fades out on its own. Details: a copper bulb, a comparator and two observers turn each rising edge into 4 ticks of full-strength signal for the loop; 6 dust carry the signal back around, losing 5 per 4-tick lap. builds.name: mono-nonretrig-ring-L14

builds.name: mono-retrig-2stage-k1
builds.caption: Gives a 116-tick output pulse after each input pulse, and a new input restarts it (a long retriggerable one-shot): each input fills a small fast loop that keeps a bigger, slower loop topped up, which then counts down; each extra pair of comparators in the big loop adds 56 ticks. Details: a copper bulb, a comparator and two observers turn each rising edge into 4 ticks of full-strength signal for stage 1, a two-comparator loop (4-tick lap) that decays 2 per lap, so its output lasts at least 28 ticks; a repeater reading it refills stage 2, a three-comparator loop (6-tick lap) that loses only 1 per lap, which then counts its 15 levels down. Why not an item timer (a hopper draining k items at 8 ticks each): refilling it takes about as long as the pulse itself, so a new input could not restart it at once; this one restarts on any 2-tick input. For one-shots of many seconds an item timer is the smaller build.

metrics: 2 gt (the shortest a real input makes)

builds.name: mono-nonretrig-2stage-k1
builds.caption: Gives one 118-tick output pulse per input pulse and ignores new inputs until it has finished (a long one-shot): the input fills a small fast loop through a gate, the small loop keeps a bigger slower loop topped up, and the big loop counts down while holding the gate shut; each extra pair of comparators in the big loop adds 56 ticks. Details: a copper bulb, a comparator, an observer and a delay-3 repeater charge stage 1 through a subtract comparator whose side is fed from between the two loops, so every edge is ignored until the output itself has ended; stage 2 is a three-comparator loop (6-tick lap) that loses only 1 per lap. Why not an item timer (a hopper draining k items at 8 ticks each): it would need the input held about as long as the pulse to load its items, where this one fires on a 2-tick input. For one-shots of many seconds an item timer is the smaller build.

builds.name: off-delay-2stage-k1
builds.caption: Keeps the output on for 108 ticks after the input turns off (a long off-delay): a small fast loop keeps a bigger, slower loop topped up, and once the input is gone the big loop counts down; each extra pair of comparators in the big loop adds 56 ticks. Details: stage 1 is a two-comparator loop (4-tick lap) that the input holds full; once the input stops it decays 2 per lap, so its output lasts at least 28 ticks. A repeater reading it powers stage 2, a three-comparator loop (6-tick lap) that loses only 1 per lap; stage 1's long output refills it evenly at full strength, and once stage 1 dies stage 2 counts its 15 levels down and the output goes dark at 0. Why not an item timer (a hopper draining k items at 8 ticks each, about 6 blocks for any length): the items move back only one per 8 ticks too, so an item timer needs an input about as long as its delay before it can time again, and it only comes in 8-tick steps; this loop refills in 3 ticks of input and keeps 2-tick resolution. For delays of many seconds an item timer is the smaller build.

Set the code from behind by turning the code frames, then turn the dials to match them: the torch at the north end, under the bus, lights (open) only when every dial shows the same position as its code frame, and never for a moment while you turn. Wire a piston door or an iron door to that torch. Inside, per dial: a comparator behind the code frame's block reads the code and powers a block beside the code dust, so the dust carries the code at full value; the dial's comparator passes the dial's value only if it is at least the code (else a torch under its dust lights), and a second comparator passes the code only if it is at least the dial's value (else a torch on its block lights). One dust line under all the torches joins every mismatch into the block under its north end, which turns the output torch off (opens within 6 ticks, closes within 8). A dial takes 3 rows; dials pair up back to back, with one empty row between pairs.

The same design as bamboo-sweeper-8x8 at the widest field one machine can sweep (10: each push moves the half's slime, observer, a 4-column wing of slime over stone blades and the other half's piston, 11 of the 12 blocks a piston can move), longer: mud over a hopper under every stalk, the 6-block two-way flying machine whose stone blades cut every stalk at its 2nd block (bamboo keeps no growth memory, so a timed cut loses nothing), walls up to y 4 along the sides and y 5 at the ends, catcher rows at both ends, and a catcher behind each end wall (an item riding on top of the machine is squeezed into the end wall as it docks, and the game moves an item stuck in a block to the closest free space, which can be behind the wall). 2,750 items smelted per hour (bamboo burns 50 gt): a double chest of ore every 1.26 h; a 10x67 field reaches full speed.

circuit.claim: the biggest harvest per block, of 3 tested
metrics: items smelted per hour per block
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: bamboo-sweeper-10x64 harvester bamboo items per hour per block 4.414, items per hour 11000.9, per cane 3.90 blocks, items per hour per cane 17.22, harvest height 7, wait 1294 gt, items smelted per hour per block 1.104, items smelted per hour 2750.2, game rts 4, bill 4372 iron, 4 quartz, 12 redstone, 92 slime, 2492 blocks, 14x7x74, robust

metrics: ~65 iron, 24 gold, ~80 redstone, 3 quartz (track and cart included)
300 items fed 5 at a time every 5 s: all delivered by 5.9 min, then the cart parked at the loader
circuit.verdict: minutes for a double chest 20.9, 2.75 items/s, 11 trips, bill 65 iron, 24 gold, 80 redstone, 3 quartz (track and cart included), 363 blocks

builds.name: ld-chest
builds.caption: The cart stops under the supply chest and pulls one item every tick: 20 items a second, a full cart in 16 seconds. It leaves when it is full, or when the chest has run empty and it holds something; an empty cart at an empty chest waits there until items come, so an idle farm's cart does not shuttle. One comparator reads the cart's fill through the detector rail; its side input is the chest's own comparator lifted to full strength by a repeater, so it passes the fill only when the cart is full or the chest is empty, and then the slope under the cart turns on. Pair it with ul-gate and 128 blocks of track (designs/circuits/rail/system/line-b.txt): a double chest delivered in 21 minutes.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: ld-chest cart-loader line terminus, load rate 16.87 items/s, departure delay 17 gt, 44 blocks, 9x4x6, robust

builds.name: station-slope-v2
builds.caption: A one-way minecart station: the track drops two blocks on two powered rails that slope down the way the carts go. Switched off, a powered rail brakes a cart hard, so every cart coming in, even at full speed, stops on the slope, ridden or empty. The button beside the lower rail (in reach from the cart) switches both rails on: the cart rolls down and is pushed out at speed.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: station-slope-v2 station 1 line one-way, stop distance 1.60 blocks, departure delay 1 gt, leaves at 0.22 b/t, 6 blocks, 3x3x2, robust

builds.name: station-slope2-v4
builds.caption: A two-way minecart station: the one-way station's two braking slopes, then a detector rail and an always-on booster. Carts going the station's way stop on the slopes and leave when the button is pressed. Carts coming the other way are sped up by the booster, cross the detector rail quickly, and it switches the slopes on long enough for them to climb straight through.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: station-slope2-v4 station 2 line two-way, stop distance 1.60 blocks, departure delay 1 gt, leaves at 0.37 b/t, other way passes at 0.40 b/t, 10 blocks, 5x3x2, robust

builds.name: cart-unloader-t3
builds.caption: A hopper-minecart unloader at the end of a line: the line comes in one block up and the cart rolls down a detector-rail slope onto a powered rail over a hopper, stopping against the end block; the hopper empties it into the chest. The powered rail switches on only when the hopper is empty and the detector has been quiet for a moment, so a loaded cart waits until its last item has gone and is then pushed back up the line; an empty cart is sent back at once. Gravity on the slope brings even a crawling cart in quickly, so no booster is needed.

circuit.claim: 9 blocks smaller, half the speed
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: cart-unloader-t3 cart-unloader line terminus, unload rate 2.48 items/s, departure delay 15 gt, 22 blocks, 5x3x3, robust

builds.name: ul-gate
builds.caption: The cart climbs a short powered slope and stops against a closed fence gate, which leaves it straddling two blocks: the hopper under the slope and the hopper beside it both pull from it, emptying a full cart in 64 seconds, twice as fast as one hopper. When the hoppers find nothing more, the slope turns on and the cart rolls back down the line. Pair it with ld-chest and 128 blocks of track (designs/circuits/rail/system/line-b.txt): a double chest delivered in 21 minutes.

circuit.claim: the fastest of 2 tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: ul-gate cart-unloader line terminus, unload rate 4.79 items/s, departure delay 14 gt, 31 blocks, 6x3x4, robust

builds.name: stick-v24
builds.caption: Crafts four sticks from every two planks. The iron block machine with seven of the crafter's slots disabled, so the planks fill the top two slots of the left column and the comparator reads 9 once two planks are in.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: stick-v24 crafter stick crafts/min 75.5, first craft by 40 gt, crafts 93 (2 waiting sets checked), hoppers awake 1, recipe class 2x2, supply items, bill 5 iron, 2 quartz, 12 redstone, 16 blocks, 4x2x3, robust

builds.name: table-v24
builds.caption: Crafts a crafting table from every four planks. The iron block machine with five of the crafter's slots disabled, so the planks fill the top-left 2x2 and the comparator reads 9 once four planks are in.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: table-v24 crafter crafting_table crafts/min 37.5, first craft by 60 gt, crafts 47 (2 waiting sets checked), hoppers awake 1, recipe class 2x2, supply items, bill 5 iron, 2 quartz, 12 redstone, 16 blocks, 4x2x3, robust

builds.name: ironblock-v24
builds.caption: Crafts an iron block from every nine iron ingots. A hopper fills the crafter one ingot per slot. A comparator reads the crafter; a second comparator, reading a crafter whose nine slots are all disabled, holds a constant 9 at its side, so it turns on only when all nine slots are full. Its signal goes round through two dust and a repeater into the stone beside the crafter, which then crafts into the chest below.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: ironblock-v24 crafter iron_block crafts/min 16.6, first craft by 100 gt, crafts 22 (2 waiting sets checked), hoppers awake 1, recipe class 3x3, supply items, bill 5 iron, 2 quartz, 12 redstone, 16 blocks, 4x2x3, robust

builds.name: tnt-a
builds.caption: Crafts a TNT block from every 5 gunpowder and 4 sand. Gunpowder and sand must go into the crafter in turn, because TNT's pattern alternates them and a crafter fills its slots in order. A comparator reads how many slots are filled; each change flips two copper bulbs, one locking the sand hopper while the count is even, the other locking the gunpowder hopper while it is odd. The second bulb also pulses the crafter, which crafts once all nine slots are full; an extra comparator keeps the sand hopper locked from the ninth item until the bulbs have flipped back after the craft.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: tnt-a crafter tnt crafts/min 18.8, first craft by 80 gt, crafts 21 (2 waiting sets checked), hoppers awake 1, recipe class multi, supply items.gunpowder + items.sand, bill 10 iron, 7 quartz, 27 redstone, 31 blocks, 5x3x5, robust

builds.name: brewer-small
builds.caption: One brewing stand in a 3x6x5 box: a clock (two hoppers passing 106 stones back and forth, a copper bulb remembering the direction) splits time into two halves of 42 seconds. When the brewing half starts, the clock's own torch flashes under the block next to the bulb, which fires two droppers beside it: one lifts a nether wart into the hoppers over the stand, the other a sugar that takes two more hoppers and so arrives later, then waits until the wart is used up: the stand brews awkward potions, then swiftness. The bottles hopper beside the stand is unlocked only in that half and the hopper under the stand only in the other, when it takes the three potions to the output chest (a repeater keeps the bottles hopper locked a moment longer when the halves change, so a fresh bottle is never taken out unbrewed). Blaze powder goes into the stand's side from the fuel chest.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: brewer-small brewer 1 potions/min per stand 1.9, first potion by 1680 gt, blaze powder 1 for 8 brews, hoppers awake 9, at rest no, a clock runs on, blocks per stand 42.0, bill 60 iron, 3 quartz, 19 redstone, 42 blocks, 3x6x5, robust

builds.name: compost-row
builds.caption: One composter a slice, as many slices side by side as there are crops to compost: the line of hoppers along the top carries the farm's mixed output; each slice's filter hopper holds its crop (41 of it and four named papers), so it takes only that crop from the line, and a comparator reading it unlocks the hopper under it for a moment whenever one more arrives. That hopper, kept full of the crop, drops one into the composter each time; the hopper under the composter pulls the bone meal out into the slice's chest. Anything no slice takes runs on to the overflow chest at the end of the line. A block on each line hopper keeps strays out (the input chest stands on the first).

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: compost-row composter 1 bone meal/h per composter 100, items composted/min 111.4, bone meal 22 from 368 items, first bone meal by 340 gt, hoppers awake 12, at rest yes, blocks per composter 18.0, tileable every 1, bill 20 iron, 1 quartz, 10 redstone, 18 blocks, 1x6x5, robust

builds.name: lift-pair-n0
builds.caption: A dropper elevator 4 blocks up (11 blocks): the hopper under the input chest feeds a column of droppers facing up, the top one pushing into the output chest. One observer clock (6 gt) fires the column: its observer at the second dropper is placed last (a player starts the clock by placing it), so its partner leads by 2 gt; a chain of observers facing down climbs from the partner a block every 2 gt, and an observer every two blocks fires the next three droppers 4 gt after the ones below (a hard-powered dropper powers the ones above and below it). A dropper also reads the power of the dropper two above (quasi-connectivity), so each group must be off whenever the group below turns off.

circuit.claim: the smallest for each height, of 4 designs tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: lift-pair-n0 item-elevator 4 items/s 2.50, first item 26 gt, at rest no, bill 5 iron, 5 quartz, 15 redstone, 11 blocks, 4x5x1, robust

builds.name: lift-bend-n0
builds.caption: A dropper elevator 5 blocks up (14 blocks): the hopper under the input chest feeds a column of droppers facing up, the top one pushing into the output chest. One observer clock (6 gt) fires the column: its observer at the second dropper fires droppers 0-2 and leads (its partner is placed last: a player starts the clock by placing it); a four-observer bend from it fires droppers 3-5 4 gt later; then a chain of observers facing down climbs a block every 2 gt and an observer every two blocks fires the next three droppers 4 gt after the ones below (a hard-powered dropper powers the ones above and below it). A dropper also reads the power of the dropper two above (quasi-connectivity), so each group must be off whenever the group below turns off.

circuit.claim: passed at every position and facing we tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: lift-bend-n0 item-elevator 5 items/s 2.50, first item 30 gt, at rest no, bill 5 iron, 7 quartz, 20 redstone, 14 blocks, 4x6x1, robust

builds.name: auto-door-raised-torch
builds.caption: Opens as you walk up, closes behind you, from either side: a stone plate in front of and behind each door column, any of them opening the whole door, their supports wired under the floor into the torches that hold classic6's pistons closed; each torch sits beside its bottom piston and powers the top one through the stone above it. 42 blocks (the obvious door is 44), no waiting even at a sprint, wherever you walk across the doorway. Stand still in the doorway and the door closes on you and hurts you (half a heart per hurt) until you step out. A mob on a plate opens it too: nothing vanilla tells a player from a mob, so put the plates where mobs can't walk. If the entrance doesn't need to be hidden, two iron doors with plates do the job in about 10 blocks.

circuit.claim: smallest of 6 tested
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: auto-door-raised-torch auto-door door 2x2, open wait 0 gt, close delay 27 gt, stop in doorway the door closes on them, 42 blocks, 8x5x3, robust

builds.name: auto-door-lock-v12
builds.caption: The fewest blocks: lock-v10 with the two tripwire rows joined by one dust line beside the door at the walkway's floor level. It runs right under the right hooks' blocks, which power the dust below them, so no wiring under the floor and no blocks to stop dust climbing where it must not.

circuit.claim: stays open for someone standing in the doorway (the pick of its kind closes on them)
circuit.verdict: CIRCUIT: auto-door-lock-v12 auto-door door 2x2, open wait 13 gt, close delay 40 gt, stop in doorway the door stays open, 91 blocks, 7x7x9, robust
